question: An investigator studying targeted therapy in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors requires a reliable test to determine the spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells in biopsy specimens. Which of the following is the most appropriate test?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "CD117-positive cells express CD117 antigen" -> "Immunohistochemistry can detect CD117 antigen in tissue samples" -> "Immunohistochemistry is the most appropriate test for spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells" -> 95%

CHAIN: "CD117-positive cells have specific genetic alterations" -> "Fluorescence in-situ hybridization can detect genetic alterations in cells" -> "Fluorescence in-situ hybridization is a suitable test for spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells" -> 90%
enhanced_information: Immunohistochemistry is the most appropriate test for determining the spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells in biopsy specimens as it can detect the CD117 antigen. This is supported by the fact that CD117-positive cells express the CD117 antigen. Fluorescence in-situ hybridization, although capable of detecting genetic alterations, is not the most suitable test for spatial distribution in this context.
analysis: Immunohistochemistry is the most appropriate test for determining the spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells in biopsy specimens as it can detect the CD117 antigen, which is expressed by CD117-positive cells. This aligns with standard medical knowledge in pathology and immunohistochemistry. While other tests like flow cytometry can detect CD117, they may not provide the spatial distribution information needed in this case. Fluorescence in-situ hybridization, although useful for genetic alterations, is not the primary choice for spatial distribution of CD117-positive cells.
